Summary  
The blog post presents an ablation study on “impact-penalty” design choices (baseline, deviation measure, discounting, and penalty function) for reinforcement-learning agents tested in several AI-Safety-Gridworld environments. Particular combinations create undesirable incentives – interference, offsetting, magnitude-insensitive side-effects, and reduced interruptibility – while other combinations (especially the stepwise-inaction baseline with Relative-Reachability or Attainable-Utility penalties) mitigate them. The knowledge fabric below links the overarching risk of unintended side-effects to these intermediate incentive mechanisms and finally to concrete training-time interventions that implement the safer design choices.

EXTRACTION CONFIDENCE[84] – fairly high; structure obeys all instructions and all nodes/edges are connected, but confidence not maximal because the post is short and some mitigating links require light inference.

Inference strategy justification  
Where the post only hints at recommended practice (e.g. “penalties with other baselines avoid interference”), I inferred the most direct intervention an AI-safety practitioner would implement (“Adopt stepwise inaction baseline …”).  All such inferences are marked with edge confidence 2.

Extraction completeness explanation  
All four failure modes analysed (interference, offsetting, magnitude-insensitive side-effects, reduced interruptibility) are captured, together with every design variable the post discusses.  Every empirical result is represented as a validating node, and every recommended or inferable fix is an intervention node, giving full causal-interventional coverage from the top-level risk to actionable training-time choices.

Key limitations  
• Fine technical detail (exact penalty equations) is not captured because the blog-level summary lacks them.  
• The maturity estimates are approximate because no deployment-scale data are given.  
• Some edges (e.g. discounting mitigating offsetting) rely on single-environment evidence, so confidence is moderate.
